summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, a new flagship model in the Opus line, claiming state-of-the-art results on several coding and knowledge-work benchmarks while matching Opus 4.8's price and becoming the default model on Claude Max and Pro.

mechanisms.reason: The document reports a step-change result on a novel-problem benchmark, well beyond incremental improvement over the prior model.
mechanisms.quote: On ARC-AGI 3 , an evaluation where the model has to solve novel problems, Opus 5’s score is three times as high as the next-best model.

mechanisms.reason: Making Opus 5 the default model on a high-volume consumer subscription surface increases the aggregate inference routed through it.
mechanisms.quote: It’s the new default model on Claude Max, and the strongest model on Claude Pro.

practices.reason: Opus 5 shows stated, benchmarked gains on coding, novel-problem reasoning and computer-use/agentic tasks that a team building coding or agent products would want to adopt.
practices.quote: Opus 5 excels on valuable software engineering tasks. For example, on Frontier-Bench v0.1, Opus 5 surpasses all other models, and more than doubles Opus 4.8’s performance at a lower cost per task.

practices.reason: Anthropic describes its own internal alignment audit and a purpose-built cyber exploit-development benchmark, both stated plainly but not directly transferable as tools an outside team could run.
practices.quote: On our automated behavioral audit, Opus 5 scores 2.3 on overall misaligned behavior, the lowest of our recent models.

practices.reason: A concrete, immediately usable API change lets developers alter available tools mid-conversation without invalidating the prompt cache, which affects how a serving pipeline is built.
practices.quote: Mid-conversation tool changes on the Claude Platform. Within a conversation, developers can now change which tools Claude can use without invalidating the prompt cache.

notable_reason: This is a major frontier model release from Anthropic with detailed, quantified capability and safety claims relative to prior models.
